_comment: Code-scanning alerts dismissed by .github/workflows/code-scanning.yml (contrib/secops/code-scanning-triage.py). One entry per tool + rule + path glob: reason is one of 'false positive', 'won't fix', 'used in tests'; comment is the argument a reviewer can check (280 characters reach GitHub). A real finding is fixed in code, never listed here.

dismissals.comment: Start-up only: Stderr.WriteString of a diagnostic just before Log.Fatal; Close of the empty log file just created; os.Remove(All) of cache files on --redownload (a missing file is normal); viper.BindPFlag, which fails only for a nil flag, and each flag is defined above it.
fnv.New64a().Write (checksum) never returns an error (hash.Hash contract), and BlockCache.Close is called only by tests before removing the files. Sync now logs its errors.

Darkside mock getrawmempool (only with --darkside-very-insecure, never on a public server): it re-parses blocks and transactions that DarksideStageBlock*/StageTransaction already parsed and accepted when the test driver staged them.

Annotated test cases for the repository's own Semgrep rules (semgrep --test, secops.yml semgrep-rule-tests); the file is never built (not in a Go package of the module's build) and the unhandled calls are the patterns under test.

binary.Write into a *bytes.Buffer of fixed-size values: bytes.Buffer.Write never returns an error (it panics only if memory is exhausted), and every value is a fixed-size integer or byte slice, so binary.Write cannot fail on encoding.

saplingHeight = int(SaplingActivationHeight): a height the node reports (int32 there). int(opts.DarksideTimeout): the operator's own --darkside-timeout in minutes, darkside test mode only. Both fit int on the 64-bit targets built.

uint64(height): height >= firstBlock >= 0 (Sapling activation). uint32(len(data)): a marshalled compact block, < 2 MB by consensus block size. int(block.Height): uint64 from the node or the checksummed cache, compared with the expected height.

uint64(getblockchaininfoReply.Blocks / EstimatedHeight): heights the node reports, int32 and non-negative there (blocks >= 0, estimatedheight >= 0); the reply comes from the operator's own node over RPC.

Node replies only (client heights are bounded by maxRequestHeight): getaddressutxos height >= 0, outputIndex < 2^31, satoshis <= MAX_MONEY; tree/tip heights >= 0; getrawtransaction -1 -> 2^64-1 is the RawTransaction.height not-main-chain sentinel. Rest: darkside.

uint64(u.ActivationHeight): an upgrade activation height from the node's getblockchaininfo (non-negative int32 there). The client-supplied amounts in EstimateCollateral/EstimateFee are now refused past MaxInt64 before the conversion.

uint64(b.GetHeight()) in ToCompact: the only callers (common.getBlockFromRPC and the darkside path) first check that GetHeight() equals the requested height >= 0; GetHeight itself returns -1 or a value <= 2^32-1.
uint8(length) in WriteCompactLengthPrefixedLen is inside `if length < 253`, and length is a len() (>= 0), so it is in [0, 252].
uint64(index) in ToCompact: index is the transaction's position in its block from Block.ToCompact's range loop (>= 0).
testclient is the upstream stress/test client, not built into the image or shipped (Dockerfile builds lightwalletd and lwdinfo); the converted values are its own command-line arguments.
Test-data generator (testtools, not shipped): string(rune(curHeight)) only feeds a fake merkle-root hash; any value, even an invalid rune, is fine for that.

DarksideStageBlocks / StageTransactionsURL fetch the URL the darkside test driver names; that is the RPC's purpose. The darkside service exists only with --darkside-very-insecure (a mock node for wallet tests that stops after 30 minutes), never on a public server.
copyFile copies the cache's own lengths/blocks files to their -corrupted names; the paths are --data-dir (operator config) joined with fixed file names, never client input.
zap is a developer tool that corrupts one byte of the file named on its command line to test the cache's corruption detection (not shipped); opening that path is its purpose.

GO-2026-5932 is the unmaintained advisory on golang.org/x/crypto/openpgp, with no fixed version (openpgp is unchanged in v0.58.0). Nothing imports openpgp: only ripemd160 and sha3 are vendored (vendor/modules.txt); govulncheck reports it not called.
